# RX Tracker NEXT 4.0.0-next.58

## Delivery Log archive correction

- Fixed Delivery Log archive creation so the strict request validator accepts
  the legitimate top-level `_csrf` transport field added by the authenticated
  browser fetch helper. The archive is now persisted before printing instead
  of being blocked as an unsupported request.
- Applied the same correction to audited archive reprints and Backoffice
  retention cleanup.
- Controlled-copy printing now waits for the frozen archive stylesheet, fonts,
  and browser paint. If the stylesheet cannot load, printing remains blocked
  rather than producing an unformatted spreadsheet-like copy. The stylesheet
  URL is resolved through the existing public proxy-aware application path.
- RX Records and Reports use the existing per-process build token for the
  affected scripts so browsers behind the proxy receive the corrected code.
- Reports and Backoffice now show compact archive codes, useful timestamps,
  RX counts, period, and integrity status. Full references, verification and
  artifact hashes, format version, and server selection evidence remain
  available under an expandable Evidence control.
- CSRF middleware still validates every unsafe cookie-authenticated request.
  The transport field is not included in the archive, fingerprint, or audit
  data, and arbitrary or nested fields remain rejected.
- Stored archive records and their integrity-bound carbon-copy artifacts are
  unchanged; the compact archive presentation is display-only.

## Safety

- No schema migration, configured RX Action change, or business-data rewrite.
- No Kasm, Cloudflare Access/Tunnel, CORS, cookie, HTTPS, trust-proxy, or
  FortiGate/reverse-proxy behavior change.
- Validate the compiled release on the testing server before a separately
  approved production update.
